acceptance: SignTool /pa verification and clean Windows install/update/uninstall pass.
verifiedBy: node --test scripts/release/windows/contract.full.test.mjs (4/4 pass, executed -- see commands.log). tests/release/windows.test.mjs (pre-existing, committed in 2ff0a4be, not modified by this repair) continues to cover validateReleaseManifest/signingPlan/validateReceipt, which are kept byte-for-byte in contract.mjs; it was not re-run here because this repair's dispatch instructions permit running only the specific test file this repair wrote or updated.
observed: The Windows release pipeline now delegates build and signing to RightKit end to end: `pnpm --dir apps/membrane-hub release:doctor -- --platform win` then `pnpm --dir apps/membrane-hub release:build:win` (right-release build --platform win) runs tauri build --bundles nsis, signs the declared files with Azure Artifact Signing (SHA-256, RFC3161 timestamp, signtool /dlib) via tools/rightkit/packages/release/sign-windows.mjs, hardens via RightKit's hardeningscan.mjs, and seals a schema:1 release-manifest.json. This repository's contract.mjs validateSealedManifest reads that real manifest and fails closed unless platform=win, checkpoints include signed/hardened/sealed, and an installer file entry named Membrane_<version>_x64-setup.exe with a SHA-256 hash is present (test 'validateSealedManifest requires RightKit's real sealed shape and checkpoints'). validateLifecycleReceipt additionally fails closed unless the receipt's source_commit and installer_sha256 match that sealed manifest, all four gates (signature/install/update/uninstall) are 'pass', and every expected inner-PE payload has a signtool-verify-/pa-/tw proof recorded ({name, sha256, verify: 'pass'}) -- tested against a 3-payload set (main binary + 2 Tauri externalBin sidecars) with 5 negative cases: wrong commit, wrong installer hash, a failed gate, a missing payload, and an unverified payload. minimumExpectedPayloadCount reads apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json's bundle.externalBin (read-only) to compute that minimum (3 today) directly from the app's own Tauri config rather than a hardcoded guess.
gap: Two things remain deferred to the Windows machine, per this repair's hard rules (never run cargo/pnpm/Tauri/right-release/signtool/AzureSignTool from here): (1) actually running `pnpm release:doctor` then `pnpm release:build:win` to produce a real sealed release-manifest.json and signed installer bytes, and (2) actually running signtool verify /pa /tw against the installer and each inner PE plus exercising install/update/uninstall on a clean Windows machine to produce the lifecycle receipt scripts/release/windows/verify-release.mjs validates. Both require Azure Artifact Signing credentials and a human present at the signing machine for the PIN/passkey step, and are deferred to the Book 3 final phased gate. SEPARATE, CONFIRMED GAP (not a stop-condition, a finding): apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs's targets.win.sign.files and .installer.artifacts currently name only the outer NSIS installer, and RightKit signs those files strictly after tauri build --bundles nsis has already embedded the main binary and the two externalBin sidecars inside it -- so today, even a fully successful right-release build produces a sealed manifest that proves the outer installer signed and proves nothing about the three inner PEs. verify-release.mjs will correctly FAIL CLOSED on any lifecycle receipt that does not separately prove those three payloads, rather than accepting RightKit's manifest alone as sufficient. Closing this gap at the source needs edits to apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs and apps/membrane-hub/package.json, both outside this repair's allowed scope; see docs/release/windows.md and packaging/windows/release-contract.json's innerPeCoverage block.
